newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro bourses extend gains as Paris recovers.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro bourses extend gains as Paris recovers.

text.p: European bourses shrugged off a shaky opening on Wall Street to show healthy gains on Tuesday, and Paris rallied after a poor start triggered by the strong showing of the Left in parliamentary elections.

On the foreign exchange market, the dollar climbed by nearly a pfennig, with the mark slipping against other European currencies as the French poll increased expectations of a softer European single currency.
Most attention was fixed on equities after 10 European bourses, including Frankfurt and Zurich, scored trading peaks on Monday, encouraged by a big rally in Wall Street at its last session on Friday.

Paris, which stood out on Monday by plunging four percent after the surprise first round win by left-wing parties in the National Assembly polls, recovered its nerve following Prime Minister Alain Juppe's announcement that he would quit even if the centre-right won re-election next weekend.

French shares, which started well down, were up 0.8 percent by mid-afternoon after the CAC-40 stock index suffered its biggest one-day loss in four years on Monday. The franc also firmed and bond prices were steady.
Analysts said they did not believe Juppe's decision to step down would boost the centre-right's chances in next Sunday's final vote, saying it smacked too much of panic in the centre-right coalition.
"People just figure even if it is the left in power, they will have to follow the discipline imposed by world financial markets," said one share analyst.

Others saw some immediate benefits in Juppe's move "It's good news for the market. They got rid of the most unpopular guy and it boosts their chances in the second round," said a dealer at a British brokerage in Paris.

The broker said the market was awaiting the television speech of President Jacques Chirac later in the day, adding: "He has got to be careful about what he says and avoid turning the election into a vote of confidence."
In Frankfurt, floor trade extended its bull run to end at another record close of 3,674.36 points, eclipising Monday's peak, but volumes were thin.
In after-hours electronic trade, the market ran out of steam and slipped into the minus column in mid-afternoon trade.

"We've seen as much buying as selling lately -- in fact we're net sellers at the moment. There seems to be a lot of derivatives interest around which is driving gains," said one German equities trader.
London, which was closed for a public holiday on Monday, climbed 0.7 percent in early trade, its first opportunity to react to Wall Street's record close on Friday.
The bourse put on 30.6 points to reach 4,692.4 at one stage as cash-rich institutional investors looked to buy into the market. It lost half its gains by mid-afternoon as New York fell 0.4 percent.
A weaker bonds market and worries about higher interest rates kept many participants sidelined. "Turnover has been pathetic," the head of sales and trading at a large investment bank said.
French election jitters unsettled bond markets across Europe because of worries over the future of the European economic and monetary union (EMU) following the Socialist gains in France.
"If the Socialists get back into power, the chances of EMU going ahead on time certainly will be diminished," a London trader said.
In currency markets, the dollar was boosted by the fresh uncertainty over EMU following the French vote and ahead of the next round on Sunday.

"The election results suggest, if repeated next Sunday, that you are likely to get a broader grouping towards EMU, which does suggest that the euro will be a weaker currency," said Jeremy Stretch currency strategist at NatWest Markets.
A softer euro would benefit currencies outside the system such as the dollar and the Swiss franc, analysts said.

The dollar was largely unchanged against the yen from the levels seen late on Monday, but analysts said the U.S. currency was still struggling to find its sense of direction after sinking last week to five-month lows below 112 yen on expectations of higher rates in Japan.
Elsewhere, the beleaguered Czech crown was hit hard after the central bank eliminated the band within which it had moved against a mark/dollar basket.
The crown was fixed at 19.5 to the mark, compared with the previous fix of 18.08, and 33.1 to the dollar, as against 30.5.
STOCK PRICES AT 1415 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was was up 16.5 points to 4,678.3.
The Paris.17 points at 2,668.30.
Frankfurt's DAX index closed up 16.50 points at 3674.36.
CURRENCIES AT 1415 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.6983 marks and 116.45 yen compared with 1.6899 marks and 116.33 yen in late European trade on Monday.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $343.65 ounce, compared to $343.10 in late trade on Monday. Silver was one cent down at $4.74.
